notes.heading: Weathering Processes – Overview
points: Weathering breaks rocks in-situ without transport

notes.heading: Physical (Mechanical) Weathering – Overview
points: Breakdown of rocks without chemical change
Caused by physical forces like temperature and pressure
Common in deserts and cold regions

notes.heading: Chemical Weathering – Overview
points: Involves decomposition of rocks through chemical reactions
Most active in hot and humid climates

notes.heading: Biological Weathering Processes
points: Root wedging – plant roots expand cracks
Burrowing animals loosen soil and rocks

notes.heading: Comparison of Weathering Types
points: Physical → breaks rock without change in composition
All act together in natural environments

notes.heading: Chemical Weathering – Overview
points: Breakdown of rocks through chemical reactions
Most effective in humid tropical climates

notes.heading: Solution (Dissolution)
points: No chemical change in structure required initially
Creates underground voids and karst features

notes.heading: Carbonation
points: Reaction of carbon dioxide with water forms carbonic acid
Leads to caves, sinkholes, and karst topography

notes.heading: Hydration
points: Leads to swelling and weakening of rocks

notes.heading: Oxidation
points: Red color in soils and rocks

notes.heading: Reduction
points: Occurs in waterlogged or oxygen-deficient areas

notes.heading: Combined Chemical Processes
points: Hydrolysis + oxidation common in humid regions
Hydration weakens rock for further breakdown

notes.heading: Climatic Control
points: Hot humid climate → strongest chemical weathering
Arid regions show weak chemical weathering

options: Chemical weathering is absent in humid regions

notes.heading: Physical Weathering – Overview
points: Breakdown of rocks without chemical change
Driven by mechanical forces acting on rocks
Common in deserts, mountains, and cold regions
Important in preparing material for erosion

notes.heading: Gravitational Forces
points: Causes rockfalls, landslides, and mass wasting
Major force in slope failure processes

notes.heading: Expansion and Contraction
points: Rocks expand when heated and contract when cooled
Common in deserts due to extreme temperature variation

notes.heading: Water Pressure
points: Important in coastal and humid areas

notes.heading: Unloading and Expansion
points: Deep rocks expand when pressure decreases
Leads to exfoliation domes (e.g., granite domes)

notes.heading: Temperature Changes
points: Daily and seasonal temperature variations stress rocks
Different minerals expand at different rates

notes.heading: Freezing and Thawing (Frost Action)
points: Most active in cold mountainous regions

notes.heading: Frost Wedging Process
points: Leads to scree and talus formation

notes.heading: Salt Weathering
points: Common in coastal and desert areas

notes.heading: Salt Weathering Types
points: Salt hydration – expansion of hydrated salts

notes.heading: Combined Effects
points: Multiple physical forces often act together

moderate.question: Water pressure weathering occurs when:
options: Water enters cracks and expands pressure
moderate.answer: Water enters cracks and expands pressure

notes.heading: Biological Weathering – Overview
points: Breakdown of rocks due to living organisms
Common in vegetated and soil-covered areas
Important for soil formation and landscape evolution

notes.heading: Burrowing Activity
points: Animals dig and move soil/rock material
Loosens soil and exposes fresh rock surfaces

notes.heading: Effects of Burrowing
points: Breaks compact rock and soil structure

notes.heading: Wedging (Biological Wedging)
points: Plant roots or organisms enter rock cracks
Gradual widening of cracks over time
Similar to frost wedging but biological in origin

notes.heading: Plant Root Action
points: Roots grow into joints and fractures
As roots expand, they exert pressure
Trees on cliffs often accelerate breakdown

notes.heading: Chemical Role of Plants
points: Decomposition of leaves produces organic acids

notes.heading: Climatic Influence
points: Most effective in warm and humid regions
Less effective in deserts and polar regions
Soil-rich areas show strong biological weathering

Biological weathering is best described as:
options: Combined physical and chemical influence of organisms

notes.heading: Effects of Weathering – Overview
points: Produces distinct landforms and surface features
Prepares material for erosion and soil formation
Leads to weakening and disintegration of rocks

notes.heading: Exfoliation (Flaking)
points: Removal of outer rock layers in sheets or flakes
Caused mainly by pressure release and temperature changes
Common in massive igneous rocks like granite
Leads to smooth rounded rock surfaces

notes.heading: Process of Exfoliation
points: Outer layers expand and contract faster than inner core
Outer layers peel off like onion skins

notes.heading: Exfoliation Domes
points: Symbol of deep weathering and unloading

notes.heading: Formation of Exfoliation Domes
points: Uplift and removal of overlying material

notes.heading: Significance of Weathering – Overview
points: Weathering is the foundation of all geomorphic processes
Prepares material for erosion and transport

notes.heading: Geomorphological Significance
points: Creates features like domes and cliffs

notes.heading: Soil Formation Significance
points: Weathering produces parent material for soils
Adds minerals and nutrients to soil
Helps in development of fertile land
